findings.message: Pattern-scanner matches on the four docs.python.org changelogs overridden as false positives
findings.details: Matched text: 'bpo-44945: Specialize the BINARY_ADD instruction using the PEP 659 machinery. Adds five new instructions:' followed by BINARY_ADD_ADAPTIVE, BINARY_ADD_FLOAT, BINARY_ADD_INT and two more opcode names. Read in context in the decompressed snapshots (source-0..3, entry under Python 3.11.0 alpha 1 in each changelog): a 2021 interpreter changelog line about new bytecode instructions, not text addressed to an AI agent. No other source matched, and a keyword scan of sources 0-3, 12 and 14 for 'ignore previous', 'disregard', 'AI agent' and 'do not tell/mention' found nothing relevant. The subject (chat templates) does not appear in the matched text.

findings.message: runsybil.com confirmed as RunSybil's official site and added to the allowlist
findings.details: Evidence: the GitHub organisation RunSybil lists https://runsybil.com/ as its website; the GitHub profile of the post author and issue/PR author (dariushoule, 'Darius Houle') lists @runsybil as company; the live site (https://www.runsybil.com/, fetched with a browser User-Agent, sha256 6d64fffb8ef7d7a4...) is titled 'RunSybil | Rethink Application Security', links to /blog and carries a LinkedIn company page runsybil and x.com/runsybil; the /blog index lists the post; the post is bylined 'Darius Houle, Member of Technical Staff'; CSO Online names Darius Houle as a RunSybil security researcher. It is a security vendor's blog: first-party for RunSybil's own claims, not an independent source.

content_preview.title: RunSybil Says a CPython Bug Lets Chat Templates Escape Jinja Sandboxes; Python Security Team Does Not Consider the Escape a CPython Vulnerability
content_preview.summary: RunSybil says a CPython memory bug lets model chat templates escape Jinja sandboxes; Python's security team does not consider the demonstrated escape a CPython vulnerability. The crash fix shipped in 3.13.16, 3.14.8 and 3.15.0 release candidate 2.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Security firm RunSybil says a memory-safety flaw in CPython can let a malicious AI model's chat template escape a Jinja sandbox and run code inside an inference server, according to [CSO](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4245592/cpython-flaw-exposes-ai-inference-servers-to-sandbox-escape-attacks.html), which published its report on 6 November 2026. The Python Security Response Team (PSRT) told CSO that it acknowledges "the underlying CPython bug reported by RunSybil" but does not c...

recommendations: Publish with the attached corrections record (two clarifications).
runsybil.com added to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment; RunSybil statements remain vendor statements and must stay attributed to RunSybil.
In future, say when an issue or pull-request author is the researcher whose report the article covers, and attribute a recommendation relayed by an outlet to the party the outlet names.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News article of about 1,006 words (News range 400-1,200). Separates what RunSybil says, what the CPython records show and where the accounts differ; labels the Herald's own computations and the unverified third-party statements.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 15 snapshots read from disk (sources/2026-11/<slug>/source-0..14.html.gz), all HTTP 200, no archive fallback; each decompressed sha256 re-computed and equal to the manifest value. Text extracted from the raw HTML; no summaries used. Because GitHub pages render comments and labels loosely, issue/PR/commit facts were additionally checked against the GitHub REST API (timestamps in UTC). (12) CSO Online, Gyana Swain, News, Nov 6, 2026 (masthead/byline present; not a BrandPost): memory-safety flaw; malicious model templates escape code sandboxes; Houle quote; Jinja sandbox bypass; Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with backdoored chat_template.jinja via vLLM; PoCs shared with 'multiple inference providers supporting bring-your-own-model'; PSRT response 'in a response to CSO': 'We acknowledge the underlying CPython bug reported by RunSybil ... However, we do not consider the demonstrated sandbox escape to be a CPython security vulnerability'; executing untrusted Python in a sandbox 'outside CPython's security threat model'; PSRT disputed the no-coordinated-remediation suggestion because the report went by email, not CPython's private GitHub reporting channel; patch merged to main Aug. 14; backported to 3.13, 3.14, 3.15 'as a regular bug fix rather than a security fix'; late-2028 3.12 quote; researchers recommend best-effort treatment - ALL CONFIRMED. CSO adds original reporting (the PSRT's statements to CSO, the email-versus-GitHub-channel point, the backport branches) beyond the blog post, so it is an independent outlet account, not a restatement. Two items the article labels as CSO's ('CSO adds' the PoC sharing; 'CSO reports a similar recommendation') are RunSybil statements that CSO attributes to the researchers and that the RunSybil post also makes (post says 'many inference providers') - clarification filed. (14) RunSybil blog, Nov 3, 2026, Darius Houle: generic alias, __parameters__ cache, __typing_subst__ added late, tuple_index returns -1, assert(iparam >= 0) compiled out of release builds, argitems[-1] read; 'a single exploitation path affecting CPython >= 3.14'; 3.14 tuple-hash layout; Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct backdoored chat_template.jinja, arbitrary code in the serving process with 'an inference serving engine like vLLM'; DigitalOcean 'fully contained'; AWS 'implement a mitigation in AWS Bedrock'; Hugging Face 'did not respond to our attempts to contact them in the 90-day disclosure window'; vLLM 'acknowledged our report but has not decided whether it will offer a mitigation'; Jinja maintainers 'Report this to cpython. It's problem with cpython, not with Jinja.'; CPython 'declined our request to backport our patch as a security fix to older supported versions'; 'not found an owner willing to implement a holistic solution'; 'late 2028 when it reaches its end-of-life date'; 'security fix only' recommendation - ALL CONFIRMED verbatim; the article attributes each to RunSybil and says the Herald has not verified the third-party statements. (5) CPython issue gh-155752: opened by dariushoule 2026-08-13T19:37:28Z; title and body about a crash (release build: -1 used as array index); tested 3.15, 3.14, 3.13, 3.12, 3.11; no mention of sandbox or Jinja; closed by #155761 2026-08-14T05:14:25Z; linked PRs #155761, #155770, #155771, #155772 - CONFIRMED. (6) PR gh-155761: merged 2026-08-14T05:14:24Z by JelleZijlstra; raises TypeError when the changed argument is not in __parameters__; JelleZijlstra labelled backports to 3.10-3.15 on 2026-08-13 (21:04Z); backport bot conflicts for 3.12, 3.11, 3.10; StanFromIreland removed the 3.10/3.11/3.12 labels 2026-08-16T20:38Z ('this seems like a regular bug to me'); AlexWaygood 20:50Z ('I think we usually backport crashes as far as we can since they can be security vulnerabilities; segfaults can corrupt memory, etc' - the article's quote is a verbatim leading part); StanFromIreland 20:54Z ('I don't think a bug is a vulnerability simply because it causes a segfault'; 'does not seem like something exploitable in code that may exist in the real world') - CONFIRMED. (7) PR #155770 (3.15) merged 2026-08-14T08:55:41Z by hugovk; (8) #155771 (3.14) and (9) #155772 (3.13) merged 2026-09-08T02:01:03Z and 02:01:32Z by terryjreedy - CONFIRMED; all three commit messages carry 'Co-authored-by: Darius Houle <dariushoule@gmail.com>'. (10)/(11) devguide commit 4bcdd6b (authored 2026-08-09T19:52:59Z, 'Python Security Policy: Add note on sandboxes (#1874)') adds the sentence 'CPython does not support sandboxing untrusted Python code as a security boundary, so escapes from such a sandbox are not vulnerabilities in Python and should be reported to the sandbox's developers instead.' - verbatim; the policy page says a CVE ID is assigned by the PSF CNA if the PSRT determines a report is a vulnerability - CONFIRMED. Aug 9 to Aug 13 is four days: the Herald's own count, labelled as such. (0)-(3) docs.python.org changelogs: gh-155752 'Fix a crash when a types.GenericAlias argument gains a __typing_subst__ hook after the alias parameters have been cached.' appears exactly once in each of the 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15 pages, under Core and Builtins of 3.13.16 (Release date 2026-09-30), 3.14.8 (2026-09-30) and 3.15.0 release candidate 2 (2026-09-01); the 3.12 page (newest 3.12.16, 2026-10-25) has no gh-155752 entry and no 'typing_subst' string - CONFIRMED (the Herald's own check is labelled as such). (13) python.org downloads: 3.14.8 and 3.13.16 both 'Sept. 30, 2026'; 3.12 'security', end of support 2028-10; 3.12.16 Oct. 25, 2026 - CONFIRMED. (4) Jinja docs/sandbox.rst at the pinned commit: 'The Jinja sandbox can be used to render untrusted templates.' and 'The sandbox alone is not a solution for perfect security.' - verbatim. Absence claims checked against all 15 sources: no CVE id for this bug in any source (CVE ids appear in the policy page only as process text and in unrelated changelog entries); no source reports exploitation outside RunSybil's demonstration; no Hugging Face, vLLM or Pallets statement outside what RunSybil relays (CSO only lists Pallets and Hugging Face as recipients of the disclosure); no 3.12 release containing the fix. All four absence bullets hold. Quantifier scan (jq/grep of title, summary, body): 'Each lists' (3.13.16, 3.14.8, 3.15.0rc2 - each checked, identical entry) and 'None of the cited sources' (x2) hold; 'All three comments' (all on PR #155761) holds. No relative dates; calendar dates and UTC basis stated. Independent-source recount (per outlet): 1 independent news outlet (CSO Online). Primary records not authored by RunSybil: the devguide policy page and commit, the four docs.python.org changelogs, the python.org downloads page and Jinja's sandbox docs (project documents, not reporting). RunSybil-side or RunSybil-authored: the blog post, issue gh-155752 and PR gh-155761 (opened by RunSybil's researcher); backport PRs are bot-created and merged by CPython core developers. runsybil.com allowlisted (see findings). Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article does not concern Anthropic or an Anthropic product, and no source names Anthropic in connection with this report (the only mentions are unrelated CSO sidebar headlines and a python.org sponsor list).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary and lead hold. The title's second clause matches the PSRT's own words to CSO ('we do not consider the demonstrated sandbox escape to be a CPython security vulnerability'); scope is right ('the escape', while the PSRT 'acknowledge[s] the underlying CPython bug'). Attribution is correct: the exploit mechanism, vLLM demonstration, Hugging Face/vLLM/Jinja/AWS/DigitalOcean statements are RunSybil's; the PSRT position and email-versus-GitHub-channel point are CSO's reporting; the timeline is from the CPython records. Dates, times, versions, quotes and numbers all verified (see source_verification). Two subordinate attribution/identity gaps are covered by clarifications: (1) the issue and fix author 'dariushoule' is RunSybil's Darius Houle, which the article never states; (2) 'CSO adds' / 'CSO reports a similar recommendation' present RunSybil statements as CSO's.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; uses 'says', quotes and attributes; no AI self-reference; no promotional language about the vendor.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Searched src/content/articles and submissions for RunSybil, GenericAlias and gh-155752: no prior coverage. Nearest related items (a GitLab prompt-template sandbox escape in October, CPython JIT and Brotli items) cover different events.
concerns: The author of the issue and fix (dariushoule) is RunSybil's Darius Houle; the article does not say so, so the issue, fix and blog post are one party's record, not three. Clarification filed.
'CSO adds' (proof-of-concept sharing) and 'CSO reports a similar recommendation' are RunSybil's statements relayed by CSO, which attributes them to the researchers. Clarification filed.

RunSybil is a security vendor and the central technical claims (exploit, vLLM execution, third-party responses) rest on its own post and one news report; the article states this and says the Herald has not verified the third-party responses.
Automated REJECT came from four false-positive pattern matches and the unlisted host runsybil.com; both resolved as documented in findings.
recommendations: Name the identity of an issue or PR author when it is the researcher covered.
Attribute a recommendation or claim relayed by an outlet to the party the outlet names.
editor_notes.independent_source_count: 1 independent news outlet (CSO Online); 5 CPython/Python/Jinja primary documents not authored by RunSybil; RunSybil blog, issue and fix PR are RunSybil-side.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A careful, accurately sourced News article on a contested vulnerability-classification dispute: RunSybil's claim of a CPython-based Jinja sandbox escape, the PSRT's stated position, and the fix timeline. Approved with two clarifications; the signed article is not edited. Featured candidacy: 2 - AI inference-hosting security and an open-source threat-model dispute of broad interest, though vendor-reported, without a CVE or known exploitation
